verdict: Most of the diagnosis holds up, and several of the fixes are real and cheap: a plain-BCE flag, both T4s on every run, the Ortho-all read, reading the chain on its own, and judging labels by a student's score instead of by the targets. As a 19-day schedule, though, it does not fit. (1) It needs roughly 3–5× the owner-hours it assumes. Q8 assumes ~2 h a day, yet the plan schedules ~15–20 new code paths plus 4–5 reads a day plus cloud, API and Mac queues. (2) It oversubscribes the ~4 h of Kaggle quota left before 10-09. (3) It schedules reads on Saturday and Sunday that depend on multi-weight inference, which does not exist yet. (4) It leaves the 9 h runtime of both finals unpriced. (5) Its Kaggle-only fallback overflows the 10-09 week's 30 h and lands its label and recipe evidence after its own 10-08 and 10-15 freezes. (6) Its label lab is a single paired read with a +0.008 bar against ±0.005 noise, on a ~0.88-LB ResNet. That is the same "weak proxy" pattern §1 condemns. (7) The merger path has no estimate of whether a 0.950+ team would accept a team sitting below the free 0.943 notebook. Settle cloud yes/no today. Then cut to ≤6 build items before 10-15, ≤2 new builds a day until the 10-09 reset, and finals capped by measured runtime. Without that, the realistic outcome is the plan's own "status quo" row (0.943–0.946), with more breakage.

fatal_or_major.claim: The program runs on ~2 owner-hours a day (Q8) while delivering decomposition, two finals, cloud training, an API label read, a label lab, a Mac sweep and a merger by 10-15.
fatal_or_major.problem: The engineering and attention load is several times what one person can deliver in 12 working days. In this project each new submit mode has taken about a day, with its own fixture test. The plan needs at least these new paths: chain-alone (E1a), CoAt-branch-alone (E1b), multi-weight shared-decode infer_windows (Final 2), the chain-slot swap (Final 1), fail-loud builds (E5), a per-cell timing harness behind a fake test root (E2), an I/O warmer, a cloud training launcher and env, fp16 parity checks, the API prompt, batch and parser, targets_v2 (4 sub-pieces including a masked teacher), the forum CNN recipe (new pooling, BN handling, antialias, EMA, new backbones), a slot-stratified sampler, aux heads, a sequence head plus embedding extraction, EMA, the VLM gradient diagnostic, the gold-in-training flag, and Stage B CoAtNet under DDP. That is about 1.7 builds a day with zero failures. On top of that come 4–5 LB reads a day, each needing build, push, commit-run log check, submit and ledger: about 30–45 attended minutes each, so 2.5–4 h a day on submissions alone.

verdict:
Most of the diagnosis holds up against the repo, and several of its corrections check out. Kaggle bills per session: 30 h minus the 12 h 50 min left on 10-03 is 17.2 h, which matches one 1-GPU run plus one 2-GPU run. The one-column-swap argument is right in principle. The 691→LB fit is arithmetically exact (slope 1.091, intercept −0.004, r 0.996, from fusion/runs_*/score_runs_ortho.txt). Closing the core-swap route if (A) reads < 0.947 is right. The point that the round-1 gold gate scored report+teacher is right.

The forward plan cannot run as written. (1) This week's 4–5 reads a day have no Kaggle quota for their commit runs. (2) Its own label gates are underpowered at +0.008 against an SE of ±0.005, and they contradict its own ≥0.010 rule. (3) L1 is judged on a reference the repo already says penalises exactly that change. (4) Gains are double-counted against members the public stack already holds: native384/dense/global96 CoAtNets, and ~+0.001 for blending CoAtNets. (5) The L3 API spend is gated against steven_v2 rather than the incumbent dread_soft, whose provenance is unknown. (6) Board drift and the odds are optimistic by roughly 2x. (7) The scope (~40 items, 13 kill criteria, ~95 reads, cloud + API + Mac + merger) is far beyond the throughput a solo owner has shown.

A winner would cut this to about 4 bets:
- Ortho-all, plus the chain-slot or CoAt-branch final.
- Cloud folds that serve as members, an OOF instrument and a teacher, ideally including an ImageNet-init CoAtNet.
- One label upgrade, adopted only after dread_soft's provenance is known.
- Budgeted LB reads.
